finite_definition.meaning: Number of K-element subsets of an N-element set.
finite_definition.zero_size: The empty subset is unique, so C_N^0=1, including C_0^0.
finite_definition.distinction: The family of (N+1)-element subsets of an N-element set is empty, hence its cardinality is zero. Assigning that value to the symbol C_N^(N+1) extends the retained finite notation. Neither blank triangle cells nor the existence of an empty class declares that extension.
finite_definition.falling_product_caution: Substitution K=N+1 into a longer falling product introduces a zero factor, but applying the formula beyond its established domain is an extension, not evidence that the source already defined that value.

recurrence.domain_necessity: C_n^m requires 0<=m<=n; C_n^(m+1) additionally requires m+1<=n. Their intersection is 0<=m<=n-1, implying n>=1. The right-hand coefficient is then defined.

endpoint_m_equals_n.reason: C_n^n=1 and C_(n+1)^(n+1)=1 are defined, but C_n^(n+1) is not. Thus the endpoint statement is not a well-defined finite identity; it is not a false numerical equality or a claim that 1+0 differs from 1.
endpoint_m_equals_n.empty_class_observation: At m=n the partition has one containing subset and zero non-containing subsets. This validates the counts but does not supply an already-defined out-of-range C symbol.

steps: Take an n-element set A and a new distinguished element x. Count (m+1)-element subsets of A union {x}.
Subsets containing x correspond bijectively, after removal of x, to m-element subsets of A; there are C_n^m.
Subsets not containing x are (m+1)-element subsets of A; there are C_n^(m+1).
The classes are disjoint and exhaustive. On the stated finite domain all three C symbols exist, yielding the recurrence.

proofs.method: Factorial common denominator; valid also at m=0
steps: For 0<=m<=n-1 the common denominator (m+1)!(n-m)! has nonnegative factorial arguments.
The numerator is (n+1)!, and (n+1)-(m+1)=n-m, giving C_(n+1)^(m+1).
At m=0 use 0!=1 or the unique empty subset; no ambiguous dotted product is needed.

recurrence.minimal_mathematically_certain_recommend: Keep the identity unchanged and restrict its attached range from 0<=m<=n to integer 0<=m<n (equivalently n>=1, 0<=m<=n-1). Report a domain correction to the parent; do not edit canonical source or add a silent generalized-zero convention.

E70a.source_page_local_domain: No separate n,m condition printed in the retained 0037 E70 block.
E70a.domain_necessity: The extreme left coefficients require m>=0 and m+2<=n. These conditions imply n>=2 and make all other coefficients, including the right-hand one, defined.
recurrence_proof: Apply the finite recurrence at (n,m) and (n,m+1) to obtain C_(n+1)^(m+1)+C_(n+1)^(m+2). Both applications are permitted because m+1<=n-1.
Apply it at (n+1,m+1) to obtain C_(n+2)^(m+2). Its upper-index condition m+1<=n is also satisfied.
independent_counting_proof: Adjoin two distinct new elements to an n-element set and count subsets of size m+2.
Partition by containing 2, 1 or 0 new elements. There are respectively 1, 2 or 1 choices of new elements.
The old-set selections have sizes m, m+1 and m+2, all within 0..n. The three class counts are C_n^m, 2C_n^(m+1) and C_n^(m+2). Their sum equals C_(n+2)^(m+2).
E70a.sharpness: At m<0 the first C is undefined; at m>n-2 the last left C is undefined. This domain is maximal for the written expression under the retained finite notation.
E70a.recommendation: Keep every coefficient and index unchanged; state n,m integers, n>=2 and 0<=m<=n-2 in a solution/domain clarification. Do not call this an exercise-formula erratum merely because the page locally omits a range.

E70b.source_page_local_domain: No separate n,m condition printed in the retained 0037 E70 block.
E70b.domain_necessity: The extreme left coefficients require m>=0 and m+3<=n. These conditions imply n>=3 and make every other term defined.
recurrence_proof: Use independently proved E70a at (n,m) and (n,m+1). Both are in its finite domain because m+1<=n-2.
Apply the finite recurrence at (n+2,m+2) to obtain C_(n+3)^(m+3); m+2<=n+1 ensures this application is defined.
independent_counting_proof: Adjoin three distinct new elements and count subsets of size m+3.
Partition by containing 3, 2, 1 or 0 new elements. The numbers of new-element choices are 1, 3, 3 and 1: all three, one omitted, one chosen, or none.
Choose respectively m, m+1, m+2 or m+3 old elements. All selections are in the finite domain. Summing the disjoint classes gives the stated identity.
E70b.sharpness: At m<0 the first C is undefined; at m>n-3 the last left C is undefined. No wider integer domain makes the complete written expression defined without extending notation.
E70b.recommendation: Keep the identity unchanged; state n,m integers, n>=3 and 0<=m<=n-3 in a solution/domain clarification.
